method: Project-settings Stop hook (sh script) logging verbatim stdin, then: first stop emits {"decision":"block","reason":...} exit 0; second stop emits one stderr line, exit 1. One `claude -p "Say only: PING"` invocation, model haiku. Raw stdin log and CLI stderr capture retained beside this record at authoring time.

results.stop_event_fires: VERIFIED — hook_event_name "Stop" received with session_id, transcript_path, cwd, permission_mode, last_assistant_message.
results.block_decision_reaches_model: VERIFIED — the reason instructed a one-word reply; the final model output was exactly that word (PONG). The block channel re-engages the model with the reason text.
results.stop_hook_active_flag: VERIFIED — false on the first stop, true on the subsequent stop of the same turn; suitable as the single-hold bound.
results.exit_1_stderr_nonblocking: VERIFIED non-blocking — the session completed normally (CLI exit 0, final output delivered) after the hook exited 1.
results.stderr_visibility_headless: NOT VISIBLE — the hook's stderr line did not surface in the CLI's stderr in -p mode (0 bytes captured). The observer line's USER visibility on the headless surface is therefore unestablished; interactive-surface visibility not measured here.

conclusion: The supervisor channel (decision:block + reason, bounded by stop_hook_active) is fully verified on headless Claude. The observer channel is non-blocking as documented but its stderr text was not user-visible in -p mode - the wrapper's observer line must not be assumed user-visible on headless; interactive measurement remains owed before release if observer visibility is claimed there.
caveats: Single CLI version and OS; interactive, IDE, desktop, cloud surfaces unmeasured; the flat-vs-nested additionalContext envelope question does not arise (no context-injecting output in this design).
